a.label: Cherub
a.definition: Plural cherubim, the name of certain symbolical figures frequently mentioned in Scripture. They are first mentioned in connection with the expulsion of our first parents from Eden ([Gen. 3:24](/gen#Gen.3.24)). There is no intimation given of their shape or form. b.label: Zadok
b.definition:
Righteous.

The Egyptians excelled in agriculture. And after the Israelites entered into the possession of the Promised Land, their circumstances favoured in the highest degree a remarkable development of this art. Agriculture became indeed the basis of the Mosaic commonwealth.

a.label: Music
a.definition:
Jubal was the inventor of musical instruments ([Gen. 4:21](/gen#Gen.4.21)). The Hebrews were much given to the cultivation of music. After their triumphal passage of the Red Sea, Moses and the children of Israel sang their song of deliverance ([Ex. 15](/exod#Exod.15)).

It extends far into the north in barren deserts, meeting those of Syria and Mesopotamia. It is one of the few countries of the world from which the original inhabitants have never been expelled.

b.label: Zamzummims
b.definition: A race of giants; “a people great, and many, and tall, as the Anakims” ([Deut. 2:20](/deut#Deut.2.20), [21](/deut#Deut.2.21)). b.definition:
This word has considerable latitude of meaning in Scripture. a.label: Gihon
a.definition:
A stream.

One of the four rivers of Eden ([Gen. 2:13](/gen#Gen.2.13)). It has been identified with the Nile. Others regard it as the Oxus, or the Araxes, or the Ganges. b.label: Jair

The son of Segub. He was brought up with his mother in Gilead, where he had possessions ([1 Chr. 2:22](/1chr#1Chr.2.22)). a.definition: (Heb. kahal), the Hebrew people collectively as a holy community ([Num. 15:15](/num#Num.15.15)). a.label: Chaff
a.definition: The refuse of winnowed corn. It was usually burned ([Ex. 15:7](/exod#Exod.15.7); [Isa. 5:24](/isa#Isa.5.24); [Matt. 3:12](/matt#Matt.3.12)). This word sometimes, however, means dried grass or hay ([Isa. 5:24](/isa#Isa.5.24); [33:11](/isa#Isa.33.11)). Chaff is used as a figure of abortive wickedness ([Ps. 1:4](/ps#Ps.1.4); [Matt. 3:12](/matt#Matt.3.12)). b.definition: The corners of fields were not to be reaped, and the sheaf accidentally left behind was not to be fetched away, according to the law of Moses ([Lev. 19:9](/lev#Lev.19.9); [23:22](/lev#Lev.23.22); [Deut. 24:21](/deut#Deut.24.21)). a.label: Jubilee
a.definition:
A joyful shout or clangour of trumpets, the name of the great semi-centennial festival of the Hebrews. It lasted for a year. During this year the land was to be fallow, and the Israelites were only permitted to gather the spontaneous produce of the fields ([Lev. 25:11](/lev#Lev.25.11), [12](/lev#Lev.25.12)). All landed property during that year reverted to its original owner (13-34; 27:16-24), and all who were slaves were set free (25:39-54), and all debts were remitted.

a.label: Bethel
a.definition:
House of God.

A place in Central Palestine, about 10 miles north of Jerusalem, at the head of the pass of Michmash and Ai. It was originally the royal Canaanite city of Luz ([Gen. 28:19](/gen#Gen.28.19)). The name Bethel was at first apparently given to the sanctuary in the neighbourhood of Luz, and was not given to the city itself till after its conquest by the tribe of Ephraim. b.label: Flour
b.definition:
Grain reduced to the form of meal is spoken of in the time of Abraham ([Gen. 18:6](/gen#Gen.18.6)). As baking was a daily necessity, grain was also ground daily at the mills ([Jer. 25:10](/jer#Jer.25.10)). The flour mingled with water was kneaded in kneading-troughs, and sometimes leaven ([Ex. 12:34](/exod#Exod.12.34)) was added and sometimes omitted ([Gen. 19:3](/gen#Gen.19.3)). The dough was then formed into thin cakes nine or ten inches in diameter and baked in the oven.

It is a “plunging” bird, and is common on the coasts and the island seas of Palestine. b.label: Christ
b.definition: Anointed, the Greek translation of the Hebrew word rendered “Messiah” (q.v.), the official title of our Lord, occurring five hundred and fourteen times in the New Testament. It denotes that he was anointed or consecrated to his great redemptive work as Prophet, Priest, and King of his people. He is Jesus the Christ ([Acts 17:3](/acts#Acts.17.3); [18:5](/acts#Acts.18.5); [Matt. 22:42](/matt#Matt.22.42)), the Anointed One. a.label: Psaltery
a.definition: A musical instrument, supposed to have been a kind of lyre, or a harp with twelve strings. The Hebrew word nebhel, so rendered, is translated “viol” in [Isa. 5:12](/isa#Isa.5.12) (R.V., “lute”); 14:11. In [Dan. 3:5](/dan#Dan.3.5), [7](/dan#Dan.3.7), [10](/dan#Dan.3.10), [15](/dan#Dan.3.15), the word thus rendered is Chaldaic, pesanterin, which is supposed to be a word of Greek origin denoting an instrument of the harp kind.

b.label: Wine
b.definition:
The common Hebrew word for wine is yayin, from a root meaning “to boil up,” “to be in a ferment.” Others derive it from a root meaning “to tread out,” and hence the juice of the grape trodden out. The Greek word for wine is oinos_, and the Latin _vinun. But besides this common Hebrew word, there are several others which are thus rendered.

b.label: Highway
b.definition:
A raised road for public use. Such roads were not found in Palestine; hence the force of the language used to describe the return of the captives and the advent of the Messiah ([Isa. 11:16](/isa#Isa.11.16); [35:8](/isa#Isa.35.8); [40:3](/isa#Isa.40.3); [62:10](/isa#Isa.62.10)) under the figure of the preparation of a grand thoroughfare for their march.

 During their possession of Palestine the Romans constructed several important highways, as they did in all countries which they ruled.

a.label: Covenant
a.definition:
A contract or agreement between two parties. In the Old Testament the Hebrew word berith is always thus translated. Berith is derived from a root which means “to cut,” and hence a covenant is a “cutting,” with reference to the cutting or dividing of animals into two parts, and the contracting parties passing between them, in making a covenant ([Gen. 15](/gen#Gen.15); [Jer. 34:18](/jer#Jer.34.18), [19](/jer#Jer.34.19)).
